summary: Multiplexed short streaming requests causing slot fragmentation, NVLink contention and autoscaler oscillation in Dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC LexaHealth reported sustained throughput degradation for their dedicated pool after migrating to a multiplexed streaming route (embed+generate in same request). Impact: end-to-end p95 response time for short streaming requests increased from ~120ms to 950ms and p99 spiked >3s; overall token throughput for the reserved pool dropped ~35% despite GPUs showing <60% compute utilization. Environment: Dedicated pool lexhealth-dedicated (prod-us-east), autoscale enabled with min=2 max=10.

Observed behavior: high scheduler churn (frequent GPU attach/detach for tenant slots), many short-lived microbatches (~40-200 tokens) from a single tenant, per-GPU NVLink bandwidth nearing saturation, and long queue lengths on the serving runtime causing stall/wait. Customer notes the problem began after enabling streaming multiplexing to reduce client-side latency.

Why this is a concern: the autoscaler reacts to apparent low utilization by scaling down, then shortly afterwards scales up as queues form (oscillation). Slot fragmentation occurs because short streams prevent stable batch packing, leading to many partially filled slots which increases kernel kernel-launch overhead and cross-GPU NVLink chatter.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a dedicated pool with autoscale (min=2, max=10) in us-east-1.
2) Send 800 concurrent streams that do embed+generate in a multiplexed route: each request sends 20-120 tokens, short-lived, constant arrival rate for 15 minutes.
3) Observe scheduler logs for repeated GPU attach/detach for the tenant, and runtime metrics: queue_length, batch_fill_ratio, NVLink_tx_bytes/sec.
4) Compare p50/p95/p99 and token throughput before/after enabling multiplexing.

Expected: modest improvement in latency and steady slot packing.
Observed: autoscaler cycles every ~90–180s, batch_fill_ratio drops to ~0.25, queue_length spikes, and overall throughput drops by ~30–40%.
impact: Customer production traffic affected; conversational flows time out at higher rates. Seen as elevated error retries from client (retry storms), higher billing due to reattempts, and reduced effective throughput from reserved pool. Business impact: degraded user experience for LexaHealth triage workflow; customer flagged as high priority.
logs:
Excerpt (scheduler.log 2026-03-10T02:12:30Z): 
  INFO attach_slot tenant=lexahealth slot_id=slot-7 gpu=gpu-a1
  INFO detach_slot tenant=lexahealth slot_id=slot-7 reason=idle_reap
  INFO attach_slot tenant=lexahealth slot_id=slot-12 gpu=gpu-b3
  WARN nvlink: tx_util=92% rx_util=89% gpu_pair=gpu-a1<->gpu-b3 time=2026-03-10T02:13:08Z
  WARN runtime: queue_wait_ms=1350 p99 batch_fill=0.2 tenant=lexahealth route=multiplex-embed-gen
  DEBUG autoscaler: decision=scale_down delta=-1 reason=low_compute_util tenant=lexahealth
  DEBUG autoscaler: decision=scale_up delta=+2 reason=queue_latency tenant=lexahealth

NVLink counters (metrics dashboard snapshot): nvlink_tx_bytes/s peaked at 12GiB/s (95th pct) on gpu pairs serving lexhealth. GPU util (SM) remained ~48% average.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: noisy short streams cause slot fragmentation and poor packing -> low per-GPU compute efficiency but high cross-GPU sync/communication leading to NVLink saturation. Secondary hypothesis: autoscaler thresholds tuned on compute utilization alone are insufficient for multiplexed streaming workloads and cause oscillation.

What we checked:
- Confirmed low SM utilization but high runtime queue_wait and low batch_fill_ratio.
- Verified NVLink transmit/receive spikes concurrently with queue spikes.
- Reviewed autoscaler logs: scale decisions alternate scale_down/scale_up every ~1–3 minutes.
- Looked for GPU OOMs or kernel errors: none.
- Compared tenant vs pool-wide metrics: issue localized to lexhealth tenant traffic pattern.

Temporary mitigations attempted during triage:
- Increased min capacity for lexhealth to 4 GPUs (reduced oscillation but did not fully restore throughput).
- Enabled prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (minor improvement).
- Applied short-term autoscaler cooldown increase from 60s to 180s (reduced frequency of churn).

Conclusions so far: pattern indicates packing inefficiency + cross-GPU bandwidth bottleneck; need changes in slot packing heuristics and autoscaler signals (consider queue_length or network TX as input).

2026-03-11 09:44 UTC - Ethan Cole (Assignee): Increased pool min to 4 and extended autoscaler cooldown; p95 improved from ~950ms to ~420ms and throughput recovered ~15%. Need longer-term fix.

2026-03-12 15:30 UTC - Runtime Eng (Priya Menon): Proposed scheduler change: topology-aware slot placement to reduce cross-GPU NVLink hops and a new batching heuristic that prioritizes fill ratio for short-stream routes. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8932
resolution:
Workaround in place: increased reserved min capacity to 4 and extended autoscaler cooldown to 180s for lexhealth pool; recommended LexaHealth reduce multiplexing concurrency and increase per-stream token batching where feasible. Engineering actions: 1) Implement topology-aware slot assignment to prefer intra-GPU packing for multiplexed short streams. 2) Add autoscaler signal from runtime queue_length and nvlink_tx_util to prevent scale-down while queues persist. 3) Add telemetry alert to detect low batch_fill_ratio for multiplexed routes.

Status: workaround deployed (2026-03-11); engineering changes scheduled.
